sources.density_kg_m3: judgment: loess is characteristically light and open-structured; rounded to 10 kg/m³; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.erodibility: judgment, relative to granite: cohesionless silt that gullies readily; top of the range; loose sediment, ranked above all bedrock (about 4–10) by ease of entrainment: silt and fine sand move at the lowest flow speeds, cohesive clay and coarse gravel need more (Hjulström 1935, Bull. Geol. Inst. Univ. Uppsala 25); set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.diffusivity: judgment, relative to granite: cohesionless silt; hillslope transport coefficient D of Roering, Kirchner & Dietrich 1999 (WRR 35(3):853–870), used as a linear creep multiplier and scaled by how readily the rock makes mobile soil (soil production function, Heimsath et al. 1997, Nature 388:358–361): loose and friable classes 2–5, soft sedimentary 1.2–2, crystalline 0.5–1; set in P1-12; reviewed in P1-07 against the rock map and meridian cross-sections of pipeline_quick_16k and kept (STATUS.md, P1-07)
sources.vanilla_fallback: last fallback entry (MIC rock-tag README, Fallbacks table)
sources.stone_use: judgment (P1-28, Ben's hardness tiers 2026-10-01): loose silt

notes: Loess: wind-blown silt, parent of fertile steppe soils. Lithifies to siltstone (mudstone), whose metamorphic path it takes.
